items.statement: Do not rely on a balance's built-in auto-calibration alone; also carry out external performance checks.
items.quote: The auto-calibration feature of a balance may not be relied upon to the exclusion of an external performance check (21 CFR 211.68).

items.statement: For scales with a built-in auto-calibrator, perform external performance checks periodically; these may be less frequent than for scales without that feature.
items.quote: For a scale with a built-in auto-calibrator, we recommend that external performance checks be performed on a periodic basis, but less frequently as compared to a scale without this feature.

items.statement: Set the frequency of balance performance checks according to how often the scale is used and how critical the process or analytical step is and its tolerance.
items.quote: The frequency of performance checks depends on the frequency of use of the scale and the criticality and tolerance of the process or analytical step.

items.statement: Verify the calibration of a balance's auto-calibrator periodically (commonly once a year) using NIST-traceable standards or nationally accredited equivalents used in other countries.
items.quote: the calibration of an auto-calibrator should be periodically verified—a common frequency is once a year—using National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)-traceable standards or NIST-accredited standards in use in other countries.

items.statement: Firms may choose the equipment that best fits their needs, provided it can meet the relevant CGMP requirements.
items.quote: Firms are afforded the flexibility to select equipment that best satisfies their particular needs and that is capable of meeting the relevant CGMP requirements.

items.statement: Select all equipment used in the manufacturing process so that it produces quality products in line with CGMP.
items.quote: Each firm is responsible for selecting all equipment used in their manufacturing process to produce quality products in accordance with CGMP.

items.statement: Define the appropriate intended use for each piece of equipment's operation.
items.quote: They are also responsible for selecting the appropriate intended use for the equipment's operation

items.statement: Firms may modify standard equipment designs to suit their process, as long as the modified equipment is compatible with the product being processed.
items.quote: are free to modify standard equipment designs to best suit their process and that are compatible with the product under process.

items.statement: Equipment must be of a design suitable for its intended operations and for cleaning and maintenance.
items.quote: The CGMP regulations require that equipment be of appropriate design to facilitate operations for its intended use and for cleaning and maintenance (see 21 CFR 211.63 and 211.67)

items.statement: Equipment surfaces that contact components, in-process materials or drug products must not be reactive, additive or absorptive to an extent that changes the product's safety, identity, strength, quality or purity beyond official or other established requirements.
items.quote: that any equipment surface in contact with components, in-process materials, or drug products not be reactive, additive, or absorptive so as to "alter the safety, identity, strength, quality, or purity of the drug product beyond the official or other established requirements" (see 21 CFR 211.65).

items.statement: Total organic carbon (or total carbon) testing may be used for routine residue monitoring and for cleaning validation.
items.quote: TOC or TC can be an acceptable method for monitoring residues routinely and for cleaning validation.

items.statement: Before relying on TOC, establish that a substantial amount of the contaminating material is organic and contains carbon that can be oxidised under the TOC test conditions.
items.quote: In order for TOC to be functionally suitable, it should first be established that a substantial amount of the contaminating material(s) is organic and contains carbon that can be oxidized under TOC test conditions.

items.statement: TOC may be used, where justified, for both direct surface samples and indirect rinse-water samples.
items.quote: TOC use may be justified for direct surface sample testing as well as indirect (rinse water) sample testing.

items.statement: When using TOC, attribute all detected carbon to the target compound(s) when comparing results against the established limit.
items.quote: any detected carbon is to be attributed to the target compound(s) for comparing with the established limit.

items.statement: When using TOC, keep carbon from sources other than the contaminant being removed as low as possible.
items.quote: Thus, a firm should limit background carbon (i.e., carbon from sources other than the contaminant being removed) as much as possible.

items.statement: Correct the established TOC limit, or the detected residue amount compared with the specification, for the carbon content of the target material.
items.quote: The established limit, or the amount of residue detected for comparison to the specification, should correct for the target material’s composition of carbon.

items.statement: Perform recovery studies for the residue sampling and test method, as for any cleaning method.
items.quote: As for any cleaning method, recovery studies are necessary (21 CFR 211.160(b)).

items.statement: If TOC samples are held for long periods before analysis, verify how the holding time affects accuracy and limit of quantitation.
items.quote: If TOC samples are being held for long periods of time before analysis, a firm should verify the impact of sample holding time on accuracy and limit of quantitation.
